title: How plants grow in space
purpose: Teach the Fast Plants seed-to-seed cycle, cross-pollination, and what Brassica did on Mir and the ISS, with the limits of those results.

beats.sub: A Moon garden is still untested; Alo's story is fiction

captions: Fast Plants can go from seed to new seeds in about {harvest} days.
Then pollen must travel from one plant to another; they cannot pollinate themselves.
About {pod} days later, the seeds are ripe.
On the Mir space station, Brassica plants grew from seed to seed.
Astronauts moved the pollen by hand, flower to flower.
On the ISS, Brassica greens grew under lamps for {lada_days} days.
Those plants grew in orbit, not on the Moon.
ends_on: A seed needs light, time and a partner plant. Plan for all three.
